title: Sales Dialer Pricing in 2026: Published Prices for 25 Tools
summary: What 25 sales dialers publish: per-user prices, seat minimums and which plan has the power or parallel dialer, from each vendor's own page in November 2026.
body_markdown:
Most sales dialers that publish a price publish it per user a month. On vendor pages read in November 2026, a plan with a power dialer was $49 a user a month at JustCall and $50 at Aircall, both billed annually with a seat minimum, and $60 at CallCloud billed monthly. Dialer-only tools ran from $60 to $299 a seat. Trellus Power is $99.99 and Power + Parallel is $149.99. Of the 25 tools below, 18 publish a plan price and 7 quote instead.


Trellus publishes this guide and sells one of the dialers in it. Every figure for another vendor comes from that vendor's own pricing page, help centre or terms, read on the date shown in its row, and each row links the longer guide that lists the sources. No price here comes from a review site. No vendor account was used and nothing was tested. Prices change, so check the vendor's page before you budget.


## Dialers with a published per-seat price


Each row is a published plan with a dialer: the lowest one that includes a power dialer, the parallel plan where the vendor prices it separately, or the dialer add-on where the dialer is sold on top of a plan. Prices are in US dollars per user a month unless the row says otherwise. Calling usage, phone numbers and taxes can be extra.

The rows are not like for like. Aircall, JustCall, CloudTalk, Dialpad and RingCentral sell a phone system with a dialer on a higher plan. A team that already pays for a CRM is comparing the dialer-only rows; a team replacing its phone system is comparing the others.


One tool in this series prices by the account, not the seat. HighLevel, which many people call GoHighLevel, lists Starter at $97, Unlimited at $297 and Founder at $497 a month with unlimited users, and bills calls by usage at $0.0166 a minute for outbound calls in the US and Canada. Its Power Dialer is a queue of manual call tasks with no separate fee listed, and its multi-line dialer, in private beta, is billed by usage. The detail is in the[HighLevel pricing](https://www.trellus.ai/post/gohighlevel-pricing) guide, read on November 18, 2026.

## What changes the bill beyond the seat price


The seat price is one line of the bill. These are the others that the vendor pages above put in writing.


- **Seat minimums.** Five9 lists a 50-seat minimum and Orum a nine-seat minimum. Aloware lists 10 users on iPro and 5 on uPro and xPro. Aircall needs three licenses, JustCall two, and CloudTalk Expert three. CallCloud, PhoneBurner and Trellus sell a single seat.
- **One-time fees.** HubSpot Sales Hub lists required onboarding of $1,500 on Professional and $3,500 on Enterprise.
- **The billing term.** Monthly billing costs more wherever both are listed: Aircall Professional is $50 or $70, and JustCall Pro is $49 or $69. CallCloud and Trellus list month-to-month prices only.
- **Add-ons for the dialer itself.** Apollo's power and parallel dialing need the Advanced Dialer add-on, priced per team. CloudTalk sells Power mode and Parallel mode per user on top of the plan.
- **Usage.** HighLevel bills every call by the minute. Close bills calls, texts and numbers by usage on every plan. Apollo calls use credits, at 1 credit per 30 seconds for US calls. HubSpot caps calling minutes per account each month.
- **One line or several.** A power dialer calls one number at a time. A parallel dialer calls several and connects the rep to the first person who answers. Where a vendor sells both, the parallel plan costs more: $125 against $60 at CallCloud, $149 against $99 at WAVV on monthly billing, and $149.99 against $99.99 at Trellus.


## Where Trellus sits


**Trellus** is a Chrome extension that adds power and parallel dialing inside the CRM, sales engagement platform or spreadsheet a team already uses. It works with 31 platforms. The[Trellus power dialer](https://www.trellus.ai/power-dialer) plan, Power, is $99.99 per seat per month. The[Trellus parallel dialer](https://www.trellus.ai/parallel-dialer) plan, Power + Parallel, is $149.99 and calls up to five numbers at once. Both are bought online with no seat minimum. There is no free plan or free trial, and the Business plan is custom. The plan details are on[Trellus pricing](https://www.trellus.ai/pricing) .


Several rows above cost less per seat than Trellus and include a phone system. Trellus costs more than those, sells single seats, and adds parallel dialing without replacing the CRM or sequencer a team works in. For feature-by-feature pages, see[Trellus comparisons](https://www.trellus.ai/compare) .


## Frequently asked questions


### How much does a sales dialer cost per user?


On vendor pages read in November 2026, a plan with a power dialer was $49 a user a month at JustCall and $50 at Aircall, both billed annually with a seat minimum, $60 at CallCloud billed monthly and $60 at Aloware billed annually with five users. Dialer-only tools ran from $60 to $299 a seat. Trellus Power is $99.99 and Power + Parallel is $149.99. Seven vendors in this guide quote instead.


### Which sales dialers publish their prices?


Aircall, Apollo, CallCloud, Close, CloudTalk, Dialpad, Five9, HubSpot Sales Hub, JustCall, PhoneBurner, RingCentral, Salesfinity and Trellus each publish at least one per-seat price for a plan with a dialer, and so do Aloware and WAVV. Nooks, Orum, Koncert, Kixie, ConnectAndSell, Outreach and Salesloft show no per-seat price on their own sites and ask you to request a quote.


### Does a parallel dialer cost more than a power dialer?


Yes, at the vendors that sell both and publish prices. CallCloud lists its Power Dialer at $60 and its Parallel Dialer at $125 per seat a month. Trellus lists Power at $99.99 and Power + Parallel at $149.99. WAVV lists Single Line at $99 and Multi Line at $149 on monthly billing. CloudTalk lists Power mode at $15 and Parallel mode at $39 per user on top of a plan. Salesfinity Gold, a parallel dialer, is $249 billed annually.


### Which dialers can a team buy for one or two users?


CallCloud, PhoneBurner and Trellus sell a single seat, and Salesfinity sells one to five licenses online. JustCall needs two licenses, Aircall three and Aloware five on the plan with its Power Dialer. Five9 lists a 50-seat minimum and Orum a nine-seat minimum, so a small team would be paying for seats it does not use. Check the minimum before comparing per-seat prices.


### Which dialers have a free trial?


The vendor pages list a 14-day trial at JustCall, CloudTalk, Close and Dialpad, 7 days at Aircall, Aloware, Kixie, Quo and WAVV, three business days at CallCloud and a trial with no credit card at PhoneBurner. Trellus has no free plan or free trial. Five9, Nextiva and Salesfinity list no trial, and the quote-only vendors do not publish one. Trial limits vary, so read the terms on each page.
